servers.access: Runs local analysis tooling on your own machine and reads the files and artifacts you point it at; it executes the REA toolchain locally, with no hosted component.
servers.description: Reverse-engineering toolkit — native binaries, managed and Electron apps, firmware, and web targets — exposed as MCP tools for agents.
servers.name: rea
servers.title: REA
servers.why: The engine behind this collection's reverse-engineer-anything pick, callable directly over MCP; the curator's own RE workhorse, in daily use.

servers.access: Acts on your GitHub account with your token's scopes — it can read and write anything that token can, so scope the token to the job.
servers.description: GitHub's official MCP server: repositories, issues, pull requests, and Actions from any MCP client.
servers.name: github
servers.title: GitHub MCP Server
servers.why: The first-party reference integration — the fastest way to give an agent real, scoped GitHub access; this repo's own pipeline runs on it.

servers.access: Acts on your Cloudflare account with the OAuth scopes or API token you grant — it can read and change anything those permissions allow, across your zones, Workers and storage.
servers.description: Cloudflare's official MCP server for the entire Cloudflare API — Workers, KV, D1, R2, DNS and the rest — behind one remote endpoint.
servers.name: cloudflare
requires: Cloudflare account — OAuth sign-in or an API token
servers.title: Cloudflare API MCP Server
servers.why: The curator's whole bot fleet runs on Cloudflare, and this is the first-party server Cloudflare's own docs recommend for operating it.

servers.access: Sends your library and topic queries to Context7's hosted index and returns documentation; read-only — it runs nothing on your machine and touches no accounts.
servers.description: Live, version-specific documentation lookup: pulls current docs and code examples for libraries and frameworks straight into the agent's context.
servers.name: context7
requires: Optional Context7 API key for higher rate limits
servers.title: Context7
servers.why: Kills the stale-docs failure mode when coding against fast-moving APIs — the curator's daily stack (Workers, KV, D1) changes faster than any model's training data.

servers.access: Sends your queries and target URLs to Exa's hosted API and returns results and page content; it reaches only Exa's service — no local execution, no account access.
servers.description: Exa's official MCP server: web search, content fetching and crawling, and multi-step research through the Exa API.
servers.name: exa
servers.title: Exa MCP Server
servers.why: The shelf's single web-data slot — one key covers search plus page content, which is exactly the shape of the curator's constant source-checking work, and the free tier covers vetting-scale use.

servers.access: Launches a real browser on your machine and drives it — navigation, clicks, typing, form submissions, page JavaScript — reaching whatever sites that browser profile is signed in to.
servers.description: Microsoft's MCP server for browser automation, driving a real browser through Playwright's accessibility tree instead of screenshots.
servers.name: playwright
servers.title: Playwright MCP
servers.why: The reference browser-automation server — the standard way to give an agent hands on live web UIs for testing and verification.
